items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: So that was just kind of a fluke that we played on that record because I knew the producer and the producer was going to be in L.A.

ctx.x: I couldn’t agree more. His subject matter too, like there were no just like silly love songs, they were, the topics were very deep and the production, the whole shebang. I had a question about “Wouldn’t It Be Good” there’s that line there [scats]. Horns are playing that and is there a guitar playing with that?

It was, so the original thing for Nik Kershaw was this producer said, “Why don’t we have some horns on your record.” And Nik Kershaw said, “Okay, let’s try it.” And the producer said, “What if we play the guitar solo?” So it was an original guitar solo so I took the guitar solo off and we played to the guitar solo. So, and then we also did, I said, you know they had these other songs [scats] that one you know so we did a couple of other songs, “Let the Drums Do the Talking.” Brilliant. So that was just kind of a…

When you read the minutiae about certain recordings I’m amazed that like Al Jarreau song “Breaking Away” I was just reading the minutiae about this and you know they had eight keyboard players and two guitars and two basses and horns and recorded in three or four different studios. I don’t have a question there but it’s amazing.
